To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a system of uniform legal disposal and recycling subsidies is no longer feasible, and (2) a system of differential collection services is optimal (and implementable) when heterogeneous households can be identified on the basis of location.

(1) in the absence of heterogeneous households, an implementable policy requires a uniform collection service provision, and (2) when heterogeneous households are present, a uniform provision of collection services is not optimal and an optimal policy is implementable if and only if the households are identifiable.

a) the optimal policy is a system of uniform legal disposal subsidies and differential consumption taxes and differential recycling subsidies; b) this policy is not implementable if the households are heterogeneous, i.e. the households are different in their distaste of the waste stock and their location to the landfill; c) the optimal policy, if the households are heterogenous, is differential legal disposal subsidies and a differential provision of waste collection services.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a model of household solid waste management in which heterogeneous households differ in their distastes for the waste stock.
the analysis of the impact of heterogeneous households on the design of an efficient policy in the context of solid waste management.
the optimal provision of solid waste services and with the identification of the optimal policy to induce households to behave in a way that is optimal from a social point of view.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the optimal provision of waste collection services in the presence of heterogeneous consumers is a function of the distance to the landfill site.

, in order to attain the optimal allocation of resources, it is necessary to have differential consumption taxes, differential legal disposal subsidies and differential recycling subsidies, and to have a differential provision of refuse collection services.

the optimal policy requires differential provision of solid waste collection services and that this policy is feasible only if the households are identifiable on the basis both of their distaste for waste and their distance to the landfill site.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the presence of heterogeneous individuals, an optimal policy requires a differential provision of solid waste services.
a system of differential provision of collection is necessary to internalize the externalities generated by waste production and disposal.
the optimal policy for a heterogeneous population is to provide a differential collection service, which, if not implementable, is replaced by a differential subsidy scheme.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the presence of heterogeneous consumers, the provision of waste collection services should be tailored to the specific needs of each consumer, rather than be uniform across all households, as it is currently the case.
, when heterogeneous households are considered, it is necessary to provide a differential collection frequency to induce them to socially optimally dispose of their waste.
, in the absence of differential provision of collection, a system of consumption taxes and subsidies may not be sufficient to induce households to optimally dispose of their waste.
